output.summary: The district accepts $4,100 from the Tulare County Office of Education to support its Coordinator of College and Career Pathways taking part in the 2025-26 Leadership Development Institute. The grant period is July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, which began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays BRAVE Bay Area up to $15,000 for human trafficking prevention education at two secondary schools

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,000.00

output.summary: BRAVE Bay Area, an Oakland nonprofit, is one of the partner agencies in a human trafficking youth prevention education grant program. It will help train trainers, teach a prevention curriculum at two secondary schools, and hold workshops for caregivers. The district may pay up to $15,000 for July 1 to September 30, 2025, and the work ended before the board's ratification vote.

output.headline: Accepts $1.94M from the state for the Opportunity Young Adult Career Pathway Program through March 2027

money.evidence: accepting $1,940,425.83

output.summary: The district accepts $1,940,425.83 from the California Employment Development Department, which passes the money through, to support the Opportunity Young Adult Career Pathway Program run by the Adult and Career Education office. The grant runs from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2027, spanning two years, and began before the board vote.

vendor.name: State of California, Employment Development Department

output.headline: Adds $60,000 to Aurora Environmental's contract for school mold, chemical and lead testing
output.summary: This amendment adds $60,000 to an existing agreement with Aurora Environmental Services, raising the limit from $99,000 to $159,000. The company does required science chemical surveys, mold air quality testing at school sites, and helps with lead and water testing. The term stays July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

output.headline: Pays Kingmakers of Oakland up to $10,000 for an early reading program at MLK/Lafayette Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: The board is ratifying (formally approving) a 2025-2026 agreement with Kingmakers of Oakland to create the Jegna Journey Program, an early education reading program, at MLK/Lafayette Elementary School. The agreement runs from August 11, 2025 through May 28, 2026 and costs no more than $10,000.

output.headline: Pays Destiny Arts Center up to $10,000 for weekly dance and music classes at Madison Park Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: The board is ratifying (formally approving) a 2025-2026 agreement with Destiny Arts Center to provide weekly dance and music classes for students at Madison Park Academy - Lower Campus. The agreement runs from September 2, 2025 through May 30, 2026 and costs no more than $10,000.

output.headline: Pays search firm Hazard, Young, Attea & Associates up to $150,000 to find a new superintendent

money.evidence: at a cost not to exceed $150,000.00

output.summary: The board is ratifying (formally approving) an agreement with Hazard, Young, Attea & Associates (HYA) to run the executive search for the Superintendent of Schools. The agreement refers to a request for proposals (RFP #26-164COS) and Resolution No. 2526-0186. It runs November 13, 2025 to November 13, 2026 and costs no more than $150,000.

output.headline: Moves $4,452.72 at Fremont High from teacher stipends to conference expenses
output.summary: The board is adopting a change to Fremont High School's 2025-2026 Measures N and H spending plan, as recommended by the Measures N and H Commission. It reduces the teacher stipend line from $41,562.50 by $4,452.72 to $37,109.78 and increases the conference expenses line from $3,240 by $4,452.72 to $7,692.72. The money moves within the school's plan.

output.headline: Moves $1,631.19 at Ralph J. Bunche Academy from teacher stipends to a part-time counselor
output.summary: The board is adopting a change to Ralph J. Bunche Academy's 2025-2026 Measures N and H spending plan, as recommended by the Measures N and H Commission. It reduces the teacher stipend line from $9,323.60 by $1,631.19 to $7,692.41 and increases the pupil support salaries line, which pays for hiring a counselor at one-tenth of a full-time position, from $13,759.98 by $1,631.19 to $15,391.17. The money moves within the school's plan.

output.headline: Moves $35,625 at Skyline High from coach and administrator salaries to teacher stipends
output.summary: The board is adopting a change to Skyline High School's 2025-2026 Measures N and H spending plan, as recommended by the Measures N and H Commission. It reduces the supervisor, administrator and instructional coach salaries line from $183,606.62 by $35,625 to $147,981.62 and creates a new $35,625 line for teacher salary stipends. The money moves within the school's plan.

output.headline: Moves $70,000 at Skyline High from coach and administrator salaries to teacher substitutes
output.summary: The board is adopting a change to Skyline High School's 2025-2026 Measures N and H spending plan, as recommended by the Measures N and H Commission. It reduces the supervisor, administrator and instructional coach salaries line from $147,981.62 by $70,000 to $77,981.62 and increases the teacher substitutes line from $19,695.67 by $70,000 to $89,695.67. The money moves within the school's plan.

output.headline: Confirms a community member's appointment to the school facilities bond oversight committee
output.summary: The board is ratifying the Board President's appointment of a Community at Large member to the Measures A, B and J Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee. The appointment takes effect November 13, 2025 and fills an unexpired term that ends June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Approves 2024-25 Measure G1 carryover funding requests for named schools
output.summary: The board is adopting Resolution No. 2526-0187, which accepts the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation to approve the 2024-2025 carryover funding request for named schools. Measure G1 is the districtwide teacher retention and middle school improvement measure. The text does not list the schools or any dollar amounts.
